restatements.text: Allows individuals who are 21 or older and legally allowed to possess a handgun to carry it concealed without needing a permit.
Requires sheriffs to keep issuing concealed carry permits to qualified individuals who request them so they can be used in other states.

analysis.answer: Current law requires a person to complete an eight-hour safety course and obtain a permit from the county sheriff to carry a concealed handgun. The measure removes the permit and safety course requirements for concealed carry, while continuing to offer voluntary permits for out-of-state use.

The number of people carrying concealed handguns will likely increase as the time and cost barriers of a safety course and permit application are removed. Some individuals will continue to apply for voluntary permits to maintain concealed-carry reciprocity in other states.

Individuals aged 21 or older who can lawfully possess a handgun gain the ability to carry concealed without seeking government permission. Providers of the previously required eight-hour firearm safety courses will likely lose business.

The effect of permitless concealed carry laws on crime and public safety is disputed. Some researchers find that removing permit and training requirements increases violent crime, while others find no statistically significant effect.
